1.explanation: The TableToolbarMenu component is responsible for rendering the overflow menu button in the table toolbar. It passes the iconDescription prop to the title attribute on OverflowMenu (rendering the visible “Settings” label) but does not forward that same description to the aria-label on the underlying button (which defaults to “Menu”). Because the accessible name and visible label must match or contain each other, TableToolbarMenu’s render function needs to pass iconDescription through to OverflowMenu’s aria-label (e.g. via an ariaLabel prop) so the accessible name matches the visible “Settings” text.
1.bug_scenario: In the DataTable with toolbar story the overflow menu button shows a visible tooltip/title of “Settings” but its accessible name (aria-label) is “Menu,” triggering an IBM 2.5.3 Label in Name violation because the aria-label does not contain the visible label text.

2.explanation: The TableToolbarMenu component is responsible for rendering the overflow (settings) menu in the DataTable toolbar. It wraps the OverflowMenu and passes the iconDescription prop into the title attribute (visible tooltip) but does not use that same prop for aria-label, resulting in mismatched accessible name vs. visible text. Updating TableToolbarMenu to ensure the iconDescription is applied consistently for both title and aria-label (or otherwise surface the visible label text to assistive technology) will resolve the IBM 2.5.3 violation.
2.bug_scenario: In the DataTable “With toolbar” story, the overflow menu “Settings” icon in the toolbar is rendered as an icon-only button with an aria-label of “Menu” and a visible title of “Settings.” Because the visible label (“Settings” from the title attribute) doesn’t match the programmatic name (“Menu” from aria-label), IBM 2.5.3 Label in Name is violated.
